quizName: DMV Practice Test #12 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, you should:

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely so they can move freely.
Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough area.
Ride without a helmet because it might slip down and cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to stay in control.
questions.explanation: On rough surfaces, grip the handlebars firmly. This keeps your motorcycle pointed in the right direction.

questions.question: When riding in a group, motorcyclists:

options.text: Do not need extra space around them.
Should increase the space around them.
Should use half their normal space.
Should keep enough space around them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should keep enough space around them.
questions.explanation: In a group, ride close together but keep enough space around each rider for safety.

questions.question: Which formation helps keep group riders close together?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close while giving each rider enough safety space. Use single-file when turning, taking curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake, front or rear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when slowing down or stopping.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best way to stay close while keeping safe distance is to ride:
questions.explanation: A staggered formation keeps riders close together while giving each rider safe space. Use single-file when turning, riding curves, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:

options.text: Stay farther away from other vehicles.
Not use your high beam headlight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: At night, it is harder to judge distance. Slow down and increase your following distance. Use your high beam unless you are meeting or following another vehicle.

questions.question: If you shift into a lower gear too fast, what could happen?

options.text: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may slide.
Your motorcycle may jerk and the front tire may slide.
Your motorcycle may jerk and a warning light may turn on.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may slide.
questions.explanation: Shifting to a lower gear too quickly causes the motorcycle to jerk and the rear tire to slide, making you lose control. Slow down before shifting to a lower gear.

questions.question: The body gets rid of about one drink per hour. If someone drinks seven drinks in three hours, how many drinks are likely still in their system three hours after the last drink?
questions.explanation: To find how many drinks remain, subtract the hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. Example: seven drinks in three hours means four drinks still remain three hours later.

questions.question: Which of the following gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection as a face shield.

questions.question: A danger of braking too hard is:

options.text: Losing grip on one or both tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Losing grip on one or both tires.
questions.explanation: Braking too hard can cause one or both tires to lose grip and slide, which can cause you to crash.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while you are riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is not flat.
Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Relax your grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake on the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handlebars firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the motorcycle straight. Brake slowly on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road, squeeze the clutch, and stop.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT reduce your chance of having an accident?

options.text: Spotting hazards and deciding which ones to handle first.
Keeping space between you and other vehicles.

questions.explanation: To avoid accidents, stay alert and ready to react. Spot hazards and decide which to handle first. Always use your headlight to be more visible. Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle at all times.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straight road?

options.text: It is easier than braking on a straight road.
It is harder than braking on a straight road.
It is safe to use only the front brake.
It is safe to use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than braking on a straight road.
questions.explanation: Braking in a turn is harder than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you must know the right technique and be very careful.

questions.question: What kind of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Which of the following should a face shield NOT be?
questions.explanation: A good face shield should be free of scratches, clear on both sides, and fastened securely. It should allow air to pass through. An airtight face shield will fog up and make it hard to see.

questions.question: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
The motorcycle may speed up too much.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle may jerk and the rear tire may skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift to a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will jerk and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: What happens to face shields and goggles over time?

options.text: They never need to be replaced.
They get scratched and become brittle, so they need to be replaced often.
They should be made of material that breaks easily during a crash.
They should not allow air to pass through.

questions.correctAnswerText: They get scratched and become brittle, so they need to be replaced often.
questions.explanation: Face shields and goggles are made of plastic. Over time, they get scratched and become brittle. Replace them regularly to stay safe and comfortable.

questions.question: What should a passenger never do?
questions.explanation: Passengers under 21 in South Carolina must wear a helmet and eye protection. All riders should wear helmets. Passengers should avoid loose clothing that might catch on the motorcycle. Passengers must always lean with the driver when turning. Passengers should never ride sidesaddle.

questions.question: What is the only thing that reduces the effects of alcohol?
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. Nothing can speed this up. The only way to reduce alcohol's effects is to wait for your body to process it.

questions.question: Should you follow other vehicles closer or farther away at night than during the day?

options.text: Keep the same distance day or night.

questions.explanation: At night, it is hard to judge distances because of poor light. You cannot see shadows and light contrasts that help you during the day. Always follow farther away at night than during the day.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often. This helps you see dangers behind you.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not a substitute for a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: Before mounting the motorcycle, your pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. A paint check is not part of a pre-ride inspection.

questions.question: If your motorcycle starts to wobble, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handlebars tight and slowly release the throttle.
questions.explanation: Do not speed up, as this makes the wobble worse. Instead, hold the handlebars tight, slow down by releasing the throttle gradually, shift your weight forward and down, and pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not use the brakes, as this can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:
questions.explanation: Most crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, just a few minutes after the rider starts.
